title: Build the first inspectable CyberAlchemy Workspace vertical
outcome: Deliver one local, read-only CyberAlchemy Workspace in which a person can browse definitions, products, projects, and ontologies, inspect their provenance and authority boundaries, and open a Project-specific surface such as Essays without collapsing projected records into interface-owned meaning.
rationale: CyberAlchemy meaning is currently distributed across governed packages. The product thesis says an ergonomic work surface should reveal the objective, state, evidence, relationships, ownership, and claim limits that matter. A small workspace vertical should make those records navigable while preserving their source owners and CAV2-D65 construction order.
scope: one Project and one inspect-only Product Capability of CyberAlchemy
four non-collapsible collections: definitions, products, projects, and ontologies
stable identity, status, meaning, owner route, provenance, boundary, claim ceiling, and source epoch on every projected record
Essays as the first project entry and the prior Essays explorer candidate as evidence only
one DomainSpec-v2 source, deterministic compiled graph, generated system ontology, and immutable realization candidate
exclusions: semantic record mutation, acceptance, promotion, registration, publication, or deletion
claiming projected source currentness beyond the displayed source epoch
treating the Workspace as the owner of Essays, definitions, products, Projects, or ontologies
runtime implementation before exact owner acceptance
network, accounts, collaboration, publication, release, deployment, or external effects
owner_route: CyberAlchemy Workspace Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus DomainSpec v2 owner plus CyberAlchemy Workspace runtime owner

success_conditions.statement: The Workspace has one schema-valid Project, linked Goal, and parent-product Product Capability with distinct identities.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Project and Goal close bidirectionally, appear in the Goal ontology view, and retain authority_effect none.

success_conditions.statement: The capability-local ontology preserves definitions, products, projects, and ontologies as separate source-owned collections.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: The ontology validates identity, typed relations, provenance, source epoch, owner routes, forbidden collapses, residue, and authority ceilings.

success_conditions.statement: The Workspace crosses CAV2-D65 through a deterministic DomainSpec-v2 graph and generated system ontology before implementation.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Exact semantic, DomainSpec source, compiler, graph, system ontology, and realization-candidate identities and digests close.

success_conditions.statement: A person can browse the four collections and open Essays from a clean local interface without semantic or authority mutation.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Source-generation, unit, build, accessibility, and browser evidence cover collection navigation, detail provenance, project opening, and absence of mutating controls.

evidence_requirements: Every visible record must preserve stable identity, status, meaning, owner route, provenance, boundary, claim ceiling, and source epoch.
The prior Essays semantic-explorer candidate may inform fields and obligations but grants no Workspace ownership or implementation authority.
Generated views must not become canonical definitions, ontology admission, Project authority, or product proof.
Any acceptance-bound change requires a new realization digest and owner decision.
target_horizon: first local inspect-only vertical; no deployment deadline

revision_history.change: Created the CyberAlchemy Workspace Project and first vertical Goal after correcting the earlier Essays-local ownership assumption.

challenge_route: Challenge the desired product outcome through the CyberAlchemy Workspace Project owner, parent-product meaning through the CyberAlchemy v2 product owner, construction claims through the DomainSpec v2 owner, and runtime evidence through the CyberAlchemy Workspace runtime owner.
